title: Ways to meet an attack

D0.outcome: Names the ways to answer an attack on a piece: move it, defend it, block the line, capture the attacker, or counterattack.

D1.outcome: When told 'save the piece', finds at least one move that does it.

D2.outcome: With one of its pieces attacked and no announcement, lists the ways to save it and picks one that leaves nothing else loose.

D3.outcome: Compares the options by what each leaves behind (loose pieces, new threats) and chooses the safest.

misconceptions: The only way to save an attacked piece is to move it.
Defending a piece is enough even when the attacker is worth less than the defended piece.
conditions: When a piece is attacked, list the options: move it, defend it, capture the attacker, block the line, counterattack.
An option is good only if it leaves no other piece loose.
contrasts: Defending a piece with a more valuable piece does not help when the attacker is worth less than the piece being defended.
Moves far from both the attacked piece and the attacker are not ways to save it.
